title: Midstream-silence customer escalation: oncall diagnostics, temporary mitigations, and long-term fix
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported that long-running hosted SSE requests can transition into a silent state mid-request where no further tokens are delivered and the client never receives a terminal marker. This ticket centralizes triage notes, a short-term unblock path for affected customers, reproducible test cases, and a proposed durable fix to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: Escalations from two customers using real-time chat and code-assist: user-visible streams stop producing output after 15-40s, client libraries remain connected and eventually time out; correlated with transient autoscaling events and aggressive per-tenant rate enforcement. Customers see incomplete responses and must retry requests — significant UX and revenue impact for paid flows.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use hosted API with streaming SSE enabled and set max_tokens=1024, temperature=0.7
2) Send a single request with a 6-8k token prompt designed to trigger multi-batch generation
3) Simultaneously simulate a capacity bump by scheduling a dedicated-pool node restart (in staging),
4) Observe SSE connection: server sends initial events then becomes silent without an EOF/‘done’ sentinel; client stays connected until client-level timeout
5) Capture server side logs for request_id and node handoff trace to correlate
telemetry_to_capture: per-request request_id and opaque session_id for all SSE streams
router handoff events: node_assign, node_release, node_restart timestamps
per-tenant token-bucket state around the event (tokens_left, refill_rate)
worker-side KVcache checkpoint bindings and any serialization errors
mitigation_steps: 1) Roll out emergency config to increase client-side default SSE keepalive (server sends blank heartbeat comment) to 10s for affected accounts
2) Disable aggressive per-tenant throttling for streaming routes for two impacted customers (temporary override flag),
3) Add an on-request server-side watchdog: if no token emitted in 12s, inject a lightweight progress event (".") and trigger background health check for request handler
4) Provide a customer-facing guidance doc and SDK patch (js/python) that adds an exponential reconnect with resume token logic and shows how to detect midstream-silence
5) Postmortem hold for any rollbacks performed during the emergency window
long_term_plan: A) Implement an opaque finality marker at the streaming protocol level that is idempotent and verifiable by clients (finality_token + sequence_number),

B) Introduce deterministic session pinning: once a request streaming session starts on a worker, future retries or reconnections can be directed to a compatible worker or use the session handoff protocol to avoid silent state,
C) Replace 'silent' failure modes with explicit ephemeral failure events that are surfaced to clients and logged with a unique failure_code,
D) Harden router autoscaling handoff to await worker commit points before evicting in-flight streaming handlers,
E) Create an integration test harness (stream-replayer) that exercises node restarts, per-tenant throttling, and KVcache IO to prevent regressions
acceptance_criteria: 1) No customer reports of unexplained streaming silence in the next 4 weeks after hotfix rollout
2) All streaming events include finality_token OR an explicit failure_code on termination in 100% of test runs
3) Integration test harness reproduces previous midstream-silence within CI before the fix and validates it is resolved after changes
4) Monitoring dashboard added showing last_token_timestamp percentiles per-tenant and alert if >10s for production traffic
